description: Evaluates Stage 0 Dynamic Stage Assessment & Router adherence

evals.prompt: Add WebMCP tools to this project.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the project files (package.json, routes in App.tsx, and the store) before responding, recognizes a React recipe and meal-planning app, and routes to Stage 1 by proposing 3 candidate user journeys specific to recipes and meal planning (e.g. finding recipes by ingredient or dietary tag, organizing recipes into collections or a weekly meal plan, sharing a recipe, deleting a recipe), each with an ideal outcome and autonomous boundary (e.g. public sharing or permanent deletion requires confirmation). It invites the user to pick one goal and writes no code or schemas.
assertions: The agent read evals/fixtures/recipe-app/src/App.tsx

The output proposes candidate user journeys specific to a recipe or meal-planning app (such as finding recipes, organizing into collections or meal plans, sharing, or deleting recipes) and does not propose shopping cart or checkout journeys.
The output explicitly defines or highlights autonomous boundaries for the proposed journeys, such as requiring confirmation before publicly sharing or permanently deleting a recipe.
The output invites the user to select or focus on ONE goal first (enforcing the "One Goal Per Iteration" rule).
The output does NOT write or modify application code (e.g., no useWebMCP, registerTool, or final schema generation) in this initial turn.

evals.prompt: I want to add a tool to search flights.
evals.expected_output: The agent frames flight search as a conversational user journey / goal via the Iterative Incremental Pathway, models starting states or advances to role-play simulation, avoids full portfolio ideation friction, and avoids premature code generation.
assertions: The output frames flight search as a conversational user journey / goal rather than just a raw function signature.
The output defines or identifies ideal outcomes, required context, or autonomous boundaries for flight search.
The output advances to Stage 2 (starting states) or Stage 3 (conversational role-play) for this specific goal (Iterative Incremental Pathway).
The output does NOT force the user to ideate an entire unrelated portfolio of other features.
The output does NOT immediately write tool code (useWebMCP, registerTool) or generate a final schema before role-playing.

evals.prompt: We already defined our user goals: 1) Search flights, 2) Seat selection. Let's establish starting states.
evals.expected_output: The agent routes directly to Stage 2 (Starting States Matrix), identifies functional application state dimensions, and explicitly prunes diagnostic bloat.
assertions: The output routes directly to Stage 2 (Starting States Matrix) without re-ideating goals.
The output identifies functional application state dimensions (routes, session, authentication).
The output explicitly prunes diagnostic bloat (device_battery, gpu_temp, screen_dpi).

evals.prompt: Goal is 'Order Pizza', starting state is 'empty cart on /menu'. Let's role-play the interaction.
evals.expected_output: The agent routes to Stage 3 (Turn-by-Turn Role-Playing) simulating the 6 core turn elements, adheres to tool character limits, and triggers the mandatory User Critique Loop.
assertions: The output routes to Stage 3 (Turn-by-Turn Role-Playing) simulating the 6 core turn elements.
The output respects tool character limits (names <= 30 chars, payloads <= 1,500 chars).
The output explicitly triggers the mandatory User Critique Loop (agent demeanor/tone, clarifying questions, autonomous boundaries).

evals.prompt: Here is our happy path transcript for booking a flight. How do we make it robust?
evals.expected_output: The agent routes to Stage 4 (Variations & Graceful Failure), exploring missing parameters, prerequisite errors, over-constrained queries, coreference resolution, and human confirmation hand-offs.
assertions: The output routes to Stage 4 (Variations & Graceful Failure).

The output explores missing parameters, prerequisite errors, over-constrained queries, coreference resolution, and human confirmation hand-offs for sensitive actions (confirmation on a dedicated UI, or consequentialHint: true on tools that commit the action).

evals.prompt: Here are our approved role-play transcripts. Generate the tool schemas and automated evals.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the approved role-play transcript and routes to Stage 5. It consolidates the per-entity search_issues/search_bugs and repeated move_issue/move_bug calls into polymorphic batched tools (e.g. list_items with a types array and move_items with an items array executed with Promise.all), writes What + When descriptions without jargon, sets readOnlyHint and untrustedContentHint on the listing tool (issue and bug text is reporter-authored), and offers the local evaluation gate (npx webmcp-evals local).
assertions: The output routes to Stage 5 (Tool Specs & Evals Generation).
The agent read references/evals-format.md
The agent read evals/fixtures/project-app/roleplay-triage.md

The output consolidates the per-entity search_issues/search_bugs and repeated move_issue/move_bug calls into polymorphic batched tools (e.g. list_items with a types array and move_items with an items array) rather than keeping per-entity tools.
The output enforces "What + When" descriptions, strips internal jargon, and audits annotations (readOnlyHint, consequentialHint, untrustedContentHint).
The output proactively offers the local evaluation gate (npx webmcp-evals local).

evals.prompt: I already have a schema.json defining tools for my pizza maker application. I want to generate evals.json for automated testing.
evals.expected_output: The agent routes directly to Stage 5 (Tool Specs & Evals Generation) or asks to view the existing schema.json, rather than forcing the user to redo Stage 1 (Goal Ideation) or Stage 2.
assertions: The agent routes directly to Stage 5 (Tool Specs & Evals Generation) or asks to view the existing schema.json, rather than forcing the user to redo Stage 1 (Goal Ideation) or Stage 2.

evals.prompt: Here is my schema.json for my web app. Help me implement these tools in React.
evals.expected_output: The agent routes directly to Stage 6 (Application Implementation) without re-opening conversational design, recommending use-webmcp-tool (useWebMCP), stable schema literals, and RTL mocking.
assertions: The agent read evals/fixtures/hotel-app/schema.json
The output routes directly to Stage 6 (Application Implementation) without re-opening conversational design.
The output uses use-webmcp-tool (useWebMCP), stable/hoisted schema literals, and RTL mocking.
The agent read references/react-patterns.md
The agent did NOT read references/angular-patterns.md

evals.prompt: I want to add WebMCP tools to example.com. Where do we start?
evals.expected_output: The agent clarifies that WebMCP runs client-side in the browser tab on document.modelContext rather than external headless scraping, recommends using browser capabilities (such as the browser or page inspection or checking /llms.txt) to explore workflows, routes to Stage 1 (User Goals Portfolio) proposing candidate user journeys with autonomous boundaries, and avoids premature code dumping.
assertions: The agent read references/live-site-discovery.md
The output clarifies that WebMCP runs client-side in the browser tab on document.modelContext (requiring first-party site code or extension/content script execution).
The output does NOT confuse WebMCP with external headless scraping (Puppeteer, Playwright, or DOM clicking).
The output recommends using browser capabilities (e.g., browsing or inspecting the live pages, or checking /llms.txt) to explore the site's workflows.
The output routes to Stage 1 (User Goals Portfolio) by proposing or offering to inspect candidate user journeys with autonomous boundaries.
The output does NOT immediately output frontend code before defining goals.

evals.prompt: Can you give feedback on the tools on example.com?
evals.expected_output: The agent references inspecting live tools via document.modelContext.getTools(), the Chrome DevTools Application > WebMCP pane, or using browser inspection to inspect the live page, routes to the Stage 6 audit/review checklist rather than restarting Stage 1 ideation, audits annotations and character budgets without jargon, and suggests running the Lighthouse 'Agentic browsing' audit or DevTools manual execution.
assertions: The agent read references/audit-checklist.md
The output references inspecting live tools via document.modelContext.getTools(), the Chrome DevTools Application > WebMCP pane, or browsing/inspecting the live page.
The output routes to the Stage 6 audit/review checklist rather than restarting Stage 1 ideation from scratch.
The output mentions auditing tool annotations (specifically readOnlyHint, consequentialHint for irreversible actions, or untrustedContentHint for UGC).
The output mentions character budgets (names <= 30 chars, descriptions <= 500 chars) or removing implementation jargon.
The output suggests running the Lighthouse "Agentic browsing" audit or checking DevTools manual execution.

evals.prompt: Can you audit our existing WebMCP tools in src/tools/ for best practices and security?
evals.expected_output: The agent routes directly to Stage 6 Review Checklist & Auditing, reads references/audit-checklist.md and references/agent-security.md (plus references/error-handling.md as needed) before auditing, and systematically checks against character budgets, unhandled rejections, UI view navigation missing consequentialHint, UGC missing untrustedContentHint, and DevTools/Lighthouse readiness.
assertions: The output routes directly to Stage 6 Review Checklist & Auditing.
The agent read evals/fixtures/project-app/src/tools/project-tools.ts
The agent read references/audit-checklist.md
The agent read references/agent-security.md
The output systematically checks against character budgets (names <= 30 chars, descriptions <= 500 chars) and removing internal implementation jargon.
The output audits that tools return actionable error guidance rather than unhandled Promise rejections.
The output flags that the tab-switching tool must not declare readOnlyHint: true (it mutates UI state) and does NOT require consequentialHint: true for it.
The output audits that tools returning user-generated text declare untrustedContentHint: true.
The output verifies live inspection in the Chrome DevTools Application > WebMCP pane and running the Lighthouse "Agentic browsing" audit.

evals.prompt: Create a Python stdio MCP server for Claude Desktop to query my Postgres database.
evals.expected_output: The agent clarifies that WebMCP is specifically for client-side in-browser tools on document.modelContext, whereas backend MCP runs over stdio or SSE in Node/Python, and redirects or clarifies the protocol boundary rather than attempting to use document.modelContext in a backend environment.
assertions: The output clarifies that WebMCP is specifically for client-side in-browser tools on document.modelContext, whereas backend MCP runs over stdio or SSE in Node/Python.
The agent either redirects or clarifies the protocol boundary rather than incorrectly attempting to use document.modelContext in a Node/Python backend.
